forward_guidance.text: The 10-Q contains no quantitative guidance for fiscal Q4 2026. Qualitative statements: (1) the Company is experiencing supply constraints and rising component costs (advanced semiconductors, NAND, DRAM) and expects these trends to intensify, which may materially negatively impact revenue, costs and gross margin; price increases may not mitigate this and may reduce demand; (2) gross margins will in general be subject to volatility and downward pressure; (3) the Company intends to increase its dividend annually, subject to Board declaration; (4) the May 2026 ASRs ($10.0 billion up-front) have purchase periods ending in fiscal Q4 2026; (5) the effect of tariffs remains uncertain.
forward_guidance.source_citation: 10-Q Part I Item 2 MD&A (Macroeconomic Conditions; Tariffs and Other Measures; Gross Margin; Capital Return Program); Part II Item 2 footnote 2

key_risks.description: Component and compute supply risk: constrained supply and rising costs for advanced semiconductors, NAND and DRAM, which the Company expects to intensify. The risk factor now also covers access to cloud and AI compute capacity, with constrained supply, longer lead times and rising costs. This could hurt revenue, gross margin and AI feature availability.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II Item 1A Risk Factors; Part I Item 2 MD&A, Macroeconomic Conditions

key_risks.description: Reliance on third-party software developer support. Developers may favor larger-share platforms, and a shift to alternative distribution and payment methods could reduce App Store commissions.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II Item 1A Risk Factors. The filing lists this among the risk factors set out in this 10-Q; whether the text changed from earlier filings cannot be determined from this document.

key_risks.description: Regulatory, antitrust and litigation exposure. This includes the EU DMA (Article 6(4) preliminary findings, with possible fines up to 10% of annual worldwide net sales, and the Article 5(4) €500 million fine under appeal), the DOJ monopolization suit, and the Epic Games injunction on link-out commissions, now with a Supreme Court review of the contempt standard. DMA interoperability requirements may also prevent launching features such as Siri AI in some jurisdictions.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II Item 1 Legal Proceedings; Part II Item 1A Risk Factors. Whether this risk factor text changed from earlier filings cannot be determined from this document.

key_risks.description: Google search licensing dependence: the DOJ and Google appealed the September 2, 2025 remedies order. A reversal could impose remedies, such as barring Google from offering Apple commercial terms for search distribution, that could materially affect Apple's licensing revenue.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II Item 1A Risk Factors. Whether this risk factor text changed from earlier filings cannot be determined from this document.

key_risks.description: Tariff and trade risk: IEEPA tariffs were struck down by the Supreme Court on Feb 20, 2026 and Apple has applied for refunds (recognized as a reduction of products cost of sales). Section 301 tariffs were recently imposed, and further Section 232 semiconductor and sector tariffs remain possible. The ultimate impact is uncertain.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I Item 2 MD&A, Tariffs and Other Measures

key_risks.description: Data privacy, localization and online-safety/age-verification compliance, with heightened risk from AI features and China data localization rules.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part II Item 1A Risk Factors. Whether this risk factor text changed from earlier filings cannot be determined from this document.

key_risks.description: Supplier concentration: two vendors account for 47% and 22% of vendor non-trade receivables, and one trade customer accounts for 18% of trade receivables (carriers 27%).
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q Part I Item 1, Note 4 Financial Instruments

bull_case: Fiscal Q3 2026 net sales rose 16% to $109.4B, with growth in four of five product categories and all five geographic segments, led by iPhone (+22%), Mac (+29%) and Greater China (+22%).
Gross margin expanded to 50.1% from 46.5% (Products 40.1% vs 34.5%), and diluted EPS rose about 29% to $2.02 from $1.57.
Services grew 12% to $30.7B at a steady 75.6% gross margin, driven by advertising and cloud services.

Capital return remains very large: $25.8B of Q3 buybacks, a new $100B authorization, $10.0B of ASRs running into fiscal Q4, and net share count down to about 14.6B from 14.77B at fiscal 2025 year-end.
Cash generated by operating activities was $117.0B over nine months vs $81.8B, with $146.5B in cash and marketable securities against about $84.3B of term debt and commercial paper.
The Supreme Court granted review on the civil contempt standard in the Epic case, and the Ninth Circuit already allowed some commission on link-out purchases.
bear_case: Management expects component constraints and cost increases (memory, NAND, advanced semiconductors) to intensify, and says gross margins face volatility and downward pressure, which could erode the 50.1% margin.
Product margin gains are partly attributed to tariff refunds, which the filing does not quantify and which are likely non-recurring; the refund contribution to underlying margin is unknown.
R&D expense rose 32% (AI infrastructure and headcount), so opex is growing faster than revenue (+23% vs +16%), and compute capacity availability is a flagged risk.
Components inventory more than tripled to $7.6B (from $2.1B) and manufacturing purchase obligations total $57.0B, which could be a risk if demand softens.
iPad sales fell 6% and Wearables, Home and Accessories grew only 6%; growth is concentrated in iPhone Pro models and Mac.
Regulatory and legal overhang: DMA (possible fines up to 10% of worldwide net sales), the DOJ antitrust suit, App Store commission restrictions and Google search remedies appeals.
Price increases used to offset component costs may reduce demand, and Greater China growth benefited partly from favorable renminbi movement.

what_to_watch.text: Fiscal Q4 2026 gross margin and any management commentary on the pace of memory/NAND/DRAM cost increases, given the 10-Q says these trends are expected to intensify.
Size and persistence of tariff refunds in cost of sales, and any new Section 232 semiconductor or Section 301 tariff actions.
Services growth (advertising and cloud) and any developments on App Store commission, including the Supreme Court Epic Games review and district court remand.
R&D and AI infrastructure spending trajectory, including compute capacity access, plus the rollout of Siri AI and iOS 27 and any DMA-related regional feature withholding.
Inventory and purchase commitments: whether the components build normalizes and how the iPhone cycle compares with the prior year.
Greater China performance, which rose 22% in the quarter (64,839 over nine months, up 30%).
Completion of the $10.0B ASRs (purchase periods end in fiscal Q4 2026), the pace of repurchases against the $138.0B remaining authorization, and any dividend increase.
Tim Cook's 10b5-1 trading plan, which expires October 30, 2026, and the DMA Article 6(4) Investigation outcome.

The incremental memory and component cost impact on gross margin is not quantified in the 10-Q.
iPhone, Mac and other unit shipment data are not disclosed in the 10-Q.
Fiscal 2025 Form 10-K and fiscal Q2 2026 Form 10-Q risk factors (incorporated by reference) were not supplied, so which risk factors are truly new versus changed cannot be verified.
